channel.title: keepmum
channel.description: Releases of the keepmum Mac app

item.title: keepmum 0.1.0a14
item.description:
The fourteenth alpha of keepmum lets you turn protection on or off for Codex and Claude Code without restarting either one, and the change reaches sessions that are already open. The injection check now asks a second model before it reports a hit, and it also reads what the provider's own tools return. The Mac app has a new sidebar and Overview.
> **Alpha.** keepmum works end to end, but it has not been audited and things will change. Treat it as a safety layer, not a guarantee, and see [Limitations](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum#limitations).
## Install
1. Download `Keepmum-0.1.0a14.dmg` below, open it, and drag Keepmum into Applications. 2. Open Keepmum and follow **Setup**.
**From 0.1.0a2 through 0.1.0a13:** Keepmum updates itself if you allowed update checks (Settings › Updates › Check now). **From 0.1.0a1:** quit Keepmum and drag the new version into Applications, once.
Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
To check the download: `shasum -a 256 -c Keepmum-0.1.0a14.dmg.sha256`
## On and off take effect at once
- **Codex.** keepmum now points Codex's own OpenAI provider at itself, instead of adding a provider of its own. Codex reads that setting again for every conversation it starts or reopens, in a terminal, an editor or the Codex app, so nothing needs a restart. A conversation from before you turned protection on goes through keepmum when you reopen it. Before, it could resume straight to OpenAI, or not resume at all. A conversation that is open at the moment you switch keeps its route until it closes, and `keepmum protect` says how many are still open. Codex's web search works through keepmum, and what it sends is scanned. Both the ChatGPT login and an API key work. - **Claude Code.** Turning protection off reached only new sessions, because a running session keeps the last address it read. keepmum now writes the address explicitly, so every running session switches at once, in either direction. `keepmum include` does the same for a project you had excluded: Claude Code already open there goes back through keepmum at once, instead of carrying on straight to Anthropic, unscanned.
## The injection check
- **A second opinion.** A hit now stands only if a second model, Wolf Defender Small v2.1, also flags it. On 3,500 real tool results from Claude Code, Codex and OpenHands, the 53 flagged at Medium became 1. Catches held within about two points, except attacks planted in prodnull's repository files (46% down to 37%). It is on by default; turn it off with `keepmum guard confirm off` or on the **Checks** page. If the second model is missing or fails, the hit stands. - **Tools the provider runs.** Anthropic's web search, web fetch, code execution and MCP connector, OpenAI's web search, and Gemini's grounding run at the provider, so their results arrive inside the reply, where the check never read them. keepmum now reads them as the reply comes in, and logs a hit as a warning.
## Secrets and false masks
- **A PDF string continued over two lines** was dropped whole by keepmum's PDF reader, so a key in it went out unread. It is read and masked now. - No longer masked: a label's closing quote and the code after it (`print('KEY:', x)`), a chat channel such as `#search-rollout`, and, with personal data on, a list of city counts (`北京: 3, 上海: 2`), the text right after an email address, or the Antigravity CLI's own name for itself ("Jetski") taken for a person's.
## The app
- **One sidebar** for every page and setting: Overview and Setup; Monitor (Activity, Logs, Performance); Protection (Protection map, Masking, Tools, Checks, Extensions); Local mode (Local models, Local turns, Skills); Audit and Settings. Detection is now part of Masking. - **The Overview** opens with where protection stands and a "Needs you" list, each item opening the place that fixes it. **⌘K** finds any page, setting or action, and ⌘1 to ⌘9 open the first nine pages. - **Show masked values** on Logs and Activity (`keepmum log values on`, off by default). It asks for Touch ID or your login password first, keeps the values only in keepmum's memory, and records turning it on in the audit log. - **Extensions** has a section per agent. Each item says what it is, and you can search and filter the list. - **Setup** can restart the background service. A click on a check's mode or sensitivity shows at once. Notices slide in instead of flashing "Not connected" for a moment. On a large window, settings pages use two columns. - The **Protection map** shows the injection check on arriving replies.
This release was checked with the unit tests, the scripted suite on all five agents, and the live suite on real models: a full run on Claude Code, Codex, the Antigravity CLI, pi and opencode on Nov 21, and on Nov 22 a rerun on all five of the cases the last fixes touched.

item.title: keepmum 0.1.0a13
item.description:
The thirteenth alpha of keepmum closes five ways a secret could still reach the model provider, stops masking a long list of things that were never secret, and makes the injection check much quieter on ordinary tool output. Keepmum can now also open at login.
> **Alpha.** keepmum works end to end, but it has not been audited and things will change. Treat it as a safety layer, not a guarantee, and see [Limitations](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum#limitations).
## Install
1. Download `Keepmum-0.1.0a13.dmg` below, open it, and drag Keepmum into Applications. 2. Open Keepmum and follow **Settings › Setup**.
**From 0.1.0a2 through 0.1.0a12:** Keepmum updates itself if you allowed update checks (Settings › General › Updates › Check now). **From 0.1.0a1:** quit Keepmum and drag the new version into Applications, once.
Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
To check the download: `shasum -a 256 -c Keepmum-0.1.0a13.dmg.sha256`
## Secrets that could still reach the provider
- **A PDF the agent reads.** Claude Code and opencode send a PDF they read as the file itself, and keepmum passed files through unread, so a key printed in a vendor's onboarding PDF went out. keepmum now reads a PDF's text on your Mac. When it holds something keepmum masks, the model gets that text with the value masked, under a one-line note, in place of the file; a PDF with nothing to mask goes as it is. Codex's and the Antigravity CLI's attached PDFs are handled the same way. - **A secret that starts with `/`.** keepmum took any value after a secret's name that starts like a path for a path. About 1 in 75 keys in base64 starts with `/`, AWS secret access keys among them, and each of those was let through. A value is a path now only when it is made of named pieces, like `/run/secrets/db` or `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`. - **Part of a secret.** After keepmum had masked a key, a command that printed only part of it (`tail -c 200 .env`, or the same through `od -c`) sent that part out. A piece of 12 or more characters of a secret keepmum already masked is now masked too. - **Session cookies.** `Cookie: session=…`, `Set-Cookie`, curl's `-b`, as `curl -v` and request logs print them, had no rule. They are masked now. - **Keys written in hex**, such as a wallet's private key or an AES or HMAC key, are masked when their name says what they are, or when code turns them into bytes (`bytes.fromhex`, `Buffer.from(…, "hex")`). A transaction hash, a commit or a checksum is still left as it is.
## Fewer things masked that were never secret
Each of these went out as a placeholder, so the agent could not use it, and often stumbled over it:
- paths on your Mac, a database's host next to its password, a variable's name (`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`), a command after the word "secret", a shell default (`${TOKEN:-…}`), a URL's host next to a token in it - hashes and checksums: Docker digests, Actions pinned by commit, lockfile checksums (`h1:`, `sha512-`), transaction and block hashes, SSH key fingerprints - web search links, CSP nonces, plugin and package names, invoice and ticket numbers, request ids, regexes an agent searches with, and the agents' own tool descriptions - pictures and certificates in base64, and keepmum's own placeholders written back by the model - with personal data on: a CSV row as one value, city names, file listings and dot-files taken for names, addresses or emails
A token is now kept as a placeholder in a command only when the step that carries it goes to a host its issuer does not use. A command that also mentions another host no longer leaves a placeholder in `.env`.
## A quieter injection check
The check warned on ordinary tool output: a kubeconfig's certificate, a script's own message, a single word inside Codex's output wrapper. It now reads a tool result as the agent would: the output inside Codex's wrapper, and a long run of base64 as the text it encodes, or as a mark when it encodes none. Text the model itself wrote, read back, is not checked. A result under 200 characters needs a score of 0.40 at Medium, Low and Lowest; High keeps 0.185. On keepmum's benchmarks, every attack hidden among base64 is still caught, and AgentDojo's and LLMail's short attacks all are; about 4 in 100 of prodnull's one-line attacks now pass at Medium. The README has the numbers.
The commands check no longer reads a Python script run from a heredoc as shell, and Claude Code's own notice that it refused a write is no longer flagged. What the checks flagged is kept across restarts, so a conversation resent after a restart is not warned about again.
## The app
- **Open at login:** Settings › General › Startup. The menu bar opens when you log in; protection started at login already. - A picture the Antigravity CLI read no longer makes Google refuse the request.
This release was checked with the unit tests, the scripted suite on all five agents, and the live suite on real models. 29 real-world tasks ran on Claude Code, Codex, the Antigravity CLI, pi and opencode, several times over, and every bug above came from those runs.

item.title: keepmum 0.1.0a12
item.description:
The twelfth alpha of keepmum fixes one bug: a Codex session that sent a screenshot could stop with an error from OpenAI.
> **Alpha.** keepmum works end to end, but it has not been audited and things will change. Treat it as a safety layer, not a guarantee, and see [Limitations](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum#limitations).
## Install
1. Download `Keepmum-0.1.0a12.dmg` below, open it, and drag Keepmum into Applications. 2. Open Keepmum and follow **Settings › Setup**.
**From 0.1.0a2 through 0.1.0a11:** Keepmum updates itself if you allowed update checks (Settings › General › Updates › Check now). **From 0.1.0a1:** quit Keepmum and drag the new version into Applications, once.
Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
To check the download: `shasum -a 256 -c Keepmum-0.1.0a12.dmg.sha256`
## Fixes
- **A screenshot in a Codex tool's output could break the session.** When a tool returns an image (Codex's `view_image`, or an MCP tool that takes a screenshot), the image goes to OpenAI as base64 text. keepmum scanned that text like any other tool output. Now and then a stretch of an image's base64 looked like a secret, and keepmum put a placeholder in the middle of it. OpenAI then refused the request: `Invalid '…image_url'. Expected a base64-encoded data URL … but got an invalid base64-encoded value.` In a test on 34 real PNGs, 2 were changed this way. Images and files in a tool's output now go out as they are, as they already did in a message and in Claude Code's and the Antigravity CLI's requests. Text next to them is still masked.
A session that hit this error works again once Keepmum is updated, with no need to start a new one: keepmum changed the image only on its way out, and the agent's own copy is intact.
This release was checked with the unit tests and the scripted suite only. It was not run against real agents and models (the live suite), as earlier releases were.

item.title: keepmum 0.1.0a11
item.description:
The eleventh alpha of keepmum is about cost and two leaks. Its memory and CPU now stay flat however many requests it handles, and the local model takes about 0.2 GB of memory of its own instead of 1.7 GB. A secret a Codex script reads itself no longer reaches an MCP tool, and Codex's new image tool no longer gets real values.
> **Alpha.** keepmum works end to end, but it has not been audited and things will change. Treat it as a safety layer, not a guarantee, and see [Limitations](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum#limitations).
## Install
1. Download `Keepmum-0.1.0a11.dmg` below, open it, and drag Keepmum into Applications. 2. Open Keepmum and follow **Settings › Setup**.
**From 0.1.0a2 through 0.1.0a10:** Keepmum updates itself if you allowed update checks (Settings › General › Updates › Check now). **From 0.1.0a1:** quit Keepmum and drag the new version into Applications, once.
Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
To check the download: `shasum -a 256 -c Keepmum-0.1.0a11.dmg.sha256`
## Fixes
- **A secret a Codex script read itself could reach an MCP tool.** Codex runs a model's tool calls as one program, so a script could read `.env` with a command, pull out the token and pass it to a connector, and the token never went through keepmum. Codex's model wrote such a script on its own in testing; keepmum could only warn. keepmum writes the script Codex runs, so it now adds a check to it: a call that hands such a value to a network tool has every secret in a provider's format (GitHub, OpenAI, AWS, Slack and 74 more of keepmum's rules) replaced with `[a secret, withheld by keepmum]` as the script runs. Nothing is refused, and ordinary values go as they are. A secret with no telling shape, such as a bare password, still goes; for that keepmum warns, as before. - **Codex's image generation got real values.** Codex 0.169 offers image generation in its scripts, with API keys too. keepmum did not know the tool, so it put real values back into the prompt, which goes with any images it names to OpenAI's image service. It now keeps placeholders there, as it does for the Antigravity CLI's and opencode's image tools. - **One token in about 6,700 went unmasked.** A rule took any value with six identical characters in a row for a placeholder (`xxxxxx`), so a real token holding such a run by chance, such as about one Slack app token in 6,700, was let through. Runs now mark a placeholder only when they are at least a third of the value: of 1,520 real-format tokens with a run, 98.9% are now masked (none were), and no placeholder is. - **A file printed encoded and folded went out unmasked.** keepmum decodes a file a command prints as hex or base64, and masks it when it holds a secret. A model asked to check `.env` for hidden characters printed it as base64 folded at 8 characters a line, and as a hex dump folded so that a byte was split over two lines: keepmum read neither whole, and the token went to the provider. Lines of nothing but hex or base64 characters are now read as one, whatever their width or spacing. - **A review ran up to half a second past its deadline,** and a stopped keepmum waited up to a second. Both end on time now. After a privacy-filter request timed out, keepmum gave the stuck process 5 seconds before ending it; it ends it at once.
## Changes
- **The local model takes about 0.2 GB of memory, not 1.7 GB.** It used to copy its 1.6 GB file into its own memory. It now uses the file in place, on the GPU as on the CPU, so the weights stay in macOS's file cache, which macOS can let go when memory is short. Measured on an M5 Pro: 1,757 MB down to 210 MB (133 MB under load), starting in 250 ms instead of 560. It finds exactly what it found before, at the same speed. - **keepmum no longer grows with use.** Under steady agent traffic in a new load test (`bench/load.py`), keepmum used to take more memory and more CPU with every request: 136 MB more per 1,000 requests, and from 9 to 42 ms of CPU a request by the 2,000th. Now it uses 4.3 to 4.8 ms a request from the first to the 60,000th, and its memory levels off at about 130 to 150 MB. - keepmum keeps the 10,000 masked values used most recently. A value still in use is masked with the same placeholder every turn; one that comes back after a long pause is masked with the same placeholder too, as after a restart. - The history an agent resends with every request is no longer scanned again from the start; only values keepmum has learned since are looked for in it. - **The local model unloads after 10 minutes without a request,** as the injection and harm models already did. - **Files stay bounded.** keepmum's own log rotates at 5 MB. The audit log stays under 1 GB, about 2.8 million requests, in addition to its 90 days; when it drops its oldest entries it records that it did, so `keepmum audit verify` still checks the chain. Both now prune while keepmum runs, not only when it starts. - **Less CPU when idle:** about a fifth of what it was.
This release was checked as 0.1.0a10 was: the unit tests, the scripted suite on every agent, the live suite on real cloud models, and the Antigravity CLI live. Codex was also given the connector task five times on a real model: it read `.env` in its own script twice, and the token never reached the connector.

item.title: keepmum 0.1.0a10
item.description:
The tenth alpha of keepmum finishes the fix for Splash's first download on a new Mac. It shows how much has really come, how fast and how long is left, and offers a Hugging Face sign-in, which makes downloads faster. Splash also keeps its context across Stop and Start.
> **Alpha.** keepmum works end to end, but it has not been audited and things will change. Treat it as a safety layer, not a guarantee, and see [Limitations](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum#limitations).
## Install
1. Download `Keepmum-0.1.0a10.dmg` below, open it, and drag Keepmum into Applications. 2. Open Keepmum and follow **Settings › Setup**.
**From 0.1.0a2 through 0.1.0a9:** Keepmum updates itself if you allowed update checks (Settings › General › Updates › Check now). **From 0.1.0a1:** quit Keepmum and drag the new version into Applications, once.
Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
To check the download: `shasum -a 256 -c Keepmum-0.1.0a10.dmg.sha256`
## New
- **Faster downloads, signed in.** Hugging Face lets downloads go faster for a signed-in user. Before Splash's first download, without a token, a tip under its row in Settings › Local models offers **Get a Token** and **Add Token**. keepmum saves the token on this Mac, readable only by you, where Splash's downloader looks (`~/.cache/huggingface/token`, as `hf auth login` does). In a terminal: `keepmum guard local splash --hf-token`, which reads it on stdin. Add it before you click Start: a download that stops starts over. - **Speed and time left.** While Splash downloads, its row reads, for example, "downloading the model: 6.2 of 15.4 GB (39%), 3.1 MB/s, about 50 min left". If nothing new comes for a while, it says so, such as "nothing new for 3 min".
## Fixes
- **Splash's first download still read 0.0 GB.** 0.1.0a9 counted the file on disk, which Hugging Face's downloader writes only as the pieces it fetches at once join up. On a slower line, that file stays at 0 while gigabytes arrive. keepmum now counts what the downloader has received. In a download on a new Mac, the row climbed steadily from 0.9 to 15.2 GB, while the file on disk sat still for two minutes. - **Splash went back to a 64k context after Stop and Start.** The context you choose is now kept (`[guard] local_splash_context`). - **"Error · not_found · GET /api/tags" showed on Splash's row** for a moment as it became ready. That line was keepmum checking what server answers there, not a Splash error, and the row no longer shows it. - **0.1.0a9's notes said a stopped download picks up where it left off.** It does not: it starts over, and leaves the partial file behind. keepmum now counts only the newest one.
This release was checked as 0.1.0a9 was. The unit tests passed (1,624). The live suite on real cloud models passed 70 of 71 runs, and the Antigravity CLI passed all 17. The one failure was not keepmum: Claude Haiku would not send a token to the team channel the task asked for, so the case had nothing to check. It passed 3 of 3 when run again. A first Splash download, of 16.5 GB, was run from the app on a Mac without the model.

item.title: keepmum 0.1.0a9
item.description:
The ninth alpha of keepmum fixes local mode's first start with Splash on a new Mac, which looked stuck while it downloaded the model.
> **Alpha.** keepmum works end to end, but it has not been audited and things will change. Treat it as a safety layer, not a guarantee, and see [Limitations](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum#limitations).
## Install
1. Download `Keepmum-0.1.0a9.dmg` below, open it, and drag Keepmum into Applications. 2. Open Keepmum and follow **Settings › Setup**.
**From 0.1.0a2 through 0.1.0a8:** Keepmum updates itself if you allowed update checks (Settings › General › Updates › Check now). **From 0.1.0a1:** quit Keepmum and drag the new version into Applications, once.
Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
To check the download: `shasum -a 256 -c Keepmum-0.1.0a9.dmg.sha256`
## Fixes
- **Splash's first start showed "Fetching 1 files: 0%" for the whole download.** With Use keepmum's pick › With Splash, the first start downloads about 16.5 GB: a 1 GB draft model, then the model itself as one 15.4 GB file. Settings › Local models showed the last line of Splash's log. That line is Hugging Face's counter of *files*, which moves only when a file is done, so it read 0% from start to finish. On a new Mac it looked stuck. The row now says how much has come, such as "downloading Qwen3.6-35B-A3B…: 4.2 of 15.4 GB (27%)", then the loading and warm-up steps. - **The app stopped following a long first start after 20 minutes.** It now follows Splash until it answers, for up to 4 hours.
If a download really stops (the size stays the same), click Stop and then Start in Settings › Local models: Splash picks up where it left off.
This release was checked as 0.1.0a8 was: the unit tests, the scripted end-to-end suite, and the live suite on real models.

item.title: keepmum 0.1.0a8
item.description:
The eighth alpha of keepmum lets you look before anything a check flagged goes to the cloud, in a panel per change or the whole turn in one window. What you typed can now go back to the cloud too, with only the flagged part taken out, and each check gets its own local model setup, instructions and skills.
> **Alpha.** keepmum works end to end, but it has not been audited and things will change. Treat it as a safety layer, not a guarantee, and see [Limitations](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum#limitations).
## Install
1. Download `Keepmum-0.1.0a8.dmg` below, open it, and drag Keepmum into Applications. 2. Open Keepmum and follow **Settings › Setup**.
**From 0.1.0a2 through 0.1.0a7:** Keepmum updates itself if you allowed update checks (Settings › General › Updates › Check now). **From 0.1.0a1:** quit Keepmum and drag the new version into Applications, once.
Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
To check the download: `shasum -a 256 -c Keepmum-0.1.0a8.dmg.sha256`
## New
- **Review before it goes.** Settings › Local turns › Review first holds a hand-back until you look. A floating panel, which doesn't take the keyboard, shows what the local model wrote beside the flagged text. You can send it, edit it, ask the local model to change it, withhold a tool result, or keep the turn on your Mac. **Use the original** sends the flagged text unchanged, after a warning and a second click. `keepmum guard local handback --review`, or `keepmum review --watch` in a terminal. - **The whole turn in one window.** With Review first › Every flagged turn, one window lists every flagged piece of a turn: what you typed and each tool result. Each piece shows the original beside what goes in its place, and takes its own answer. A rewrite or summary is drafted by the local model while you look, and you can edit it, write it again or have it changed. You can also keep the original or remove the piece. Then send the turn, or keep it on your Mac. `--review turn`. - **What you typed, back to the cloud.** When the harm check keeps your message local, keepmum can send it on with the flagged part taken out: Settings › Local turns › What you typed › Local rewrite, then cloud. The rewrite may only remove words. keepmum checks that what is left is word for word from your message, and that the harm check passes it as a whole and sentence by sentence. If the local model takes out the wrong part, keepmum takes out the flagged sentences itself. The provider never gets the flagged part, in any wording. - **Settings › Local turns.** Each check has the same card: what follows a local turn, the local model it uses, and each step that model takes, with its instruction and skills. You can write your own instruction for a rewrite or summary, switch back to keepmum's without losing yours, and ask the local model to write it for you. Skills are picked per step, with a click. A skill never reaches the harm rewrite unless you pick it. - **Local models, easier.** keepmum's tested picks download with progress, from Ollama or Hugging Face. Splash runs keepmum's pick about 1.6 times as fast as Ollama, started in the background with one click. You can set the context size, how long the model stays loaded, and whether it thinks first. The Skills window asks the local model to write or change a skill. - **Protection map.** A new page draws each setting where it acts on a request, and where a hit goes. **Send a sample** shows a made-up request, with 12 kinds, take the route your settings give it. **Try a review** opens a demo of the panel or the turn window on made-up text, so you can try every answer before a real review comes up. - **Logs kept across restarts.** The Logs page shows checks and masked values in one table or split in two, with details beside the table. Its rows now outlast a restart for 30 days, without any text or previews: Settings › General › Logs page, or `keepmum log keep`. - **A color-blind safe palette**, in Settings › General.
## Changes
- **A new injection model.** The injection check now runs keepmum's fine-tune of Prompt Injection Guard Small for agent tool output. The background service downloads it once, pinned and checked. - **A review never outlasts your agent.** Measured against a server that never answers, Claude Code gives up on a request after 6 minutes and pi and opencode after 5. keepmum ends a review 10 seconds before that, so its answer still reaches the agent. The window shows how long the agent has waited. While the local model writes for you, the review pauses, for up to 2 minutes in all. - **Your answer holds for one conversation.** A message or tool result you reviewed keeps your answer in that conversation's history. If the same text comes back new, typed again or returned again, you are asked again. The only exception is within 30 seconds, for Codex's task-title request and agent retries, and the log says so. - **No local model answering is a 403**, so agents stop instead of retrying for minutes. - **Updates fall back to GitHub** when keepmum.app's feed does not load, and the Download button keeps working without it. - **keepmum says when Codex needs a restart** to go through it.
## Fixes
- **What you typed could reach the cloud unchanged.** With both checks in local mode, a turn where the injection check flagged a tool result first never had what you typed checked by the harm check. Both checks now score a turn before keepmum decides. Block mode on either refuses it with both reasons. - **One flagged text, one row and one review.** The same text twice in a request was logged twice, and Codex's task-title request opened a second review. - **A local model's tool call** is never passed to the agent. - **A piece of a flagged result** that comes back in a later one, a line or part of one, is flagged too. - **Hex bytes after a label or in a list** are decoded and scanned, so a token cannot leave as hex. - **The Skills window** now follows Settings › General › Appearance (it stayed dark). - **The engine loads all its modules at start**, so an update that swaps the app cannot break a scan in progress.
This release was checked against real agents. The unit tests passed (1,616, 96% coverage). The scripted end-to-end suite passed on Codex, Claude Code, pi, opencode and the Antigravity CLI. Every local-mode and harm case also passed on a real local model (Qwen3.6 35B). The live suite on real cloud models passed 71 of 72 runs, and the Antigravity CLI passed all 17. The one failure is a known limitation, unchanged since 0.1.0a7: Codex's model, in code mode, read a token in its own script and passed it to an MCP tool on the Mac, past keepmum. keepmum warned, as it is set to; it does not block such scripts, which would flag ordinary ones too.

item.title: keepmum 0.1.0a7
item.description:
The seventh alpha of keepmum makes local mode work for every agent, the Antigravity CLI included, and lets a conversation go back to the cloud after a planted instruction. The injection check now raises far fewer false alarms.
> **Alpha.** keepmum works end to end, but it has not been audited and things will change. Treat it as a safety layer, not a guarantee, and see [Limitations](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum#limitations).
## Install
1. Download `Keepmum-0.1.0a7.dmg` below, open it, and drag Keepmum into Applications. 2. Open Keepmum and follow **Settings › Setup**.
**From 0.1.0a2 through 0.1.0a6:** Keepmum updates itself if you allowed update checks (Settings › General › Updates › Check now). **From 0.1.0a1:** quit Keepmum and drag the new version into Applications, once.
Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
To check the download: `shasum -a 256 -c Keepmum-0.1.0a7.dmg.sha256`
## New
- **Back to the cloud after an injection.** When the injection check keeps a turn on your Mac, the rest of the conversation used to stay on the local model. Settings › Checks › After a local turn now hands it back instead. The cloud model gets the flagged result replaced: by the local model's answer, summary or rewrite (with your own instructions, if you write them), or by a notice. It never gets the result itself, and the check scans what the local model wrote before it goes. `keepmum guard local handback`. - **Skills for local turns.** Give the local model your own instructions, in Claude Code's SKILL.md format, for both checks or one. Settings › Checks › Skills for local turns, or `keepmum guard local skill add`. - **Local mode for the Antigravity CLI and Gemini CLI.** Their flagged turns used to be refused. They now go to your local server as Chat Completions, and the answer comes back in Gemini's format. - **The Antigravity CLI in Setup and Extensions.** Google moved personal Google sign-ins from Gemini CLI to the Antigravity CLI on June 18, 2026. Setup has a row for `keepmum agy`, and keepmum now watches agy's MCP servers, hooks, plugins, rules and skills for what other apps add, as it does for the other agents. What agy already had counts as yours.
## Changes
- **Fewer false alarms from the injection check.** It now defaults to Medium, and a tool result under 200 characters needs a much higher score to be flagged. On real Claude Code and Codex sessions it flags 1.7% of tool results, down from 7.8%. It still catches 97% of injections on keepmum's test set, and 85% of AgentDojo's attacks, down from 89%. A sensitivity you set yourself stays as it was; High gives the old catch rate back. - **Update checks say a little more.** To count each Mac once a day per macOS version, the day's first update check also says your Mac's macOS major version and chip (macOS 15, Apple silicon). Nothing else: no identifier, no usage data. With **Count this Mac** off (Settings › General › Updates), checks send none of it. [keepmum.app/privacy](https://keepmum.app/privacy) has the details.
## Fixes
- **Codex in local mode.** Codex now sends its tool list inside its request, and Ollama refused the whole request because of it. keepmum leaves the list out, as local mode promises no tools, and falls back to Chat Completions for a server that refuses the request's shape. - **The checks' models kept running after keepmum quit.** With the injection or harm check on, each `keepmum claude` session (or any keepmum that exited before its model went idle) could leave the model running in the background, holding 0.4 to 1 GB of memory. They now stop within two seconds of keepmum, however it ends. - **Hand-back with a summary or rewrite.** keepmum's own wording around the summary read like an injection to the check, so it never went back to the cloud. Only what the local model wrote is checked now.
This release was checked against real models: Codex, Claude Code, pi and opencode on their smallest models, and the Antigravity CLI on a Google sign-in. Every case passed but one, whose failures were the test's own: Claude Code had not been allowed to search, and a search for a placeholder found keepmum's own pages. Both were fixed, and that case and the local-mode cases were run again live after the model fix above, and passed.

item.title: keepmum 0.1.0a5
item.description:
The fifth alpha of keepmum protects the Antigravity CLI, notices what other apps add to your coding agents, and closes several ways a secret could leave your Mac in a form keepmum did not recognize. Each fix below was found by running real agents through keepmum.
> **Alpha.** keepmum works end to end, but it has not been audited and things will change. Treat it as a safety layer, not a guarantee, and see [Limitations](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum#limitations).
## Install
1. Download `Keepmum-0.1.0a5.dmg` below, open it, and drag Keepmum into Applications. 2. Open Keepmum and follow **Settings › Setup**.
**From 0.1.0a2, 0.1.0a3 or 0.1.0a4:** Keepmum updates itself if you allowed update checks (Settings › General › Updates › Check now). **From 0.1.0a1:** quit Keepmum and drag the new version into Applications, once.
Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
To check the download: `shasum -a 256 -c Keepmum-0.1.0a5.dmg.sha256`
## What's new
- **The Antigravity CLI.** `keepmum agy` starts it with every request scanned, signed in with Google or through its gateway mode. Its web tools keep placeholders, and an MCP tool it calls gets only the values that server may receive. - **What other apps add to your agents.** keepmum watches the plugins, hooks, MCP servers, skills and global instructions of Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI and opencode. When something changes, the menu bar says so (for example "Codex changed: postman@postman"). **Settings › Extensions** lists what is new, with Keep and Remove; removals and keeps appear on the Audit page. - **Secrets printed encoded are masked.** Hex dumps (`xxd`, `hexdump -C`, `od` in any layout), `od -c`, plain hex and base64 in a command's output are decoded and scanned. A block that holds a secret is masked whole, so `xxd .env` or `base64 < .env` cannot carry a key out in hex or in pieces. - **A warning for Codex scripts keepmum cannot check.** When a Codex script runs a command and hands a value it works out to a network tool, Codex shows a `keepmum: …` note after the call, the menu bar lights a dot, and macOS shows a notification. The script still runs; the hit is on the Logs page and in the audit log. - **Start, stop and restart from the menu bar.** A Background service row says what the service is doing, with Start, Stop, Restart, and Allow when Login Items needs your approval. - **The Live flow draws requests as they happen:** a request sets off as it leaves your Mac and waits at its provider until the reply arrives. - **Python 3.15.** The app's engine runs on Python 3.15.2 (was 3.12). - **Update checks and downloads go through keepmum.app**, which counts them by version and keeps no addresses. To leave your Mac out of the counts: Settings › General › Updates › Count this Mac. Updates work the same either way.
## Fixes
- **Codex scripts.** Codex 0.147 and later run commands from a JavaScript `exec` script. Its commands are now checked like any shell command, and an MCP tool the script calls gets only what its server may receive. - **opencode's Code Mode.** opencode 2.x reaches MCP servers and the web (`fetch`) from scripts, which keepmum did not know: a token could reach any MCP server or URL. Scripts now follow the same rules as Codex's. - **A password with spaces or quotes was sent in the agent's history.** keepmum puts a value back escaped for the shell (`'p@ss w0rd '\''x'\''`), and the agent sends the command it ran back to the model; that escaped form was not recognized, so it went out as it read. Every escaped form now maps back to its placeholder, and the model sees the command it wrote. - **Commands wrapped in `bash -lc '…'`.** A value is now quoted for the inner shell too. Before, a name with a space was split in two, and its halves went out in error messages; a password's `$…` was expanded. - **Masking that hid too much.** A search URL with a name in it is masked as the name only. A line's trailing `$` (`cat -A`, `sed -n l`, a grep anchor) is no longer masked with the token before it. In `grep '^GITHUB_TOKEN=' .env`, the quote after `=` is no longer read as the start of a secret. - **The Antigravity CLI's commands** get values quoted for the shell (a password with `"` broke them). - **Shutdown** no longer spins at full CPU when every warn-mode check has already finished. - **The menu panel** keeps its window to its height when a row appears or goes away.

item.title: keepmum 0.1.0a4
item.description:
The fourth alpha of keepmum can answer flagged requests with a model on your Mac instead of the cloud, lets you tune how sensitive the optional checks are, and shows what a check flagged on the Logs page.
> **Alpha.** keepmum works end to end, but it has not been audited and things will change. Treat it as a safety layer, not a guarantee, and see [Limitations](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum#limitations).
## Install
1. Download `Keepmum-0.1.0a4.dmg` below, open it, and drag Keepmum into Applications. 2. Open Keepmum and follow **Settings › Setup**.
**From 0.1.0a2 or 0.1.0a3:** Keepmum updates itself if you allowed update checks (Settings › General › Updates › Check now). **From 0.1.0a1:** quit Keepmum and drag the new version into Applications, once.
Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
To check the download: `shasum -a 256 -c Keepmum-0.1.0a4.dmg.sha256`
## What's new
- **Local mode for the injection and harm checks.** Besides Off, Warn and Block, each check can be set to **Local**. A request it flags then goes to a model on your Mac instead of the cloud provider, and your agent gets that model's answer. - The local model gets the request with its real values, which never leave your Mac. It never gets your API key, and it gets no tools, so it can only answer in text. - Later requests that still carry the flagged text stay local too, until you rewind or `/clear`. - Works with Claude Code and Codex. Gemini CLI's flagged requests are refused, as in Block. - **Several local servers.** Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp's llama-server, MLX or another server on your Mac, each with its own model, for both checks or just one. A flagged request goes to the first server that answers; if none does, it is refused, never sent. Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp take the agent's request as it is. Other servers get it as Chat Completions, and the answer goes back in the agent's own format. Settings › Checks › Local servers, or `keepmum guard local add`. - **Sensitivity for the checks.** If a check flags too much, turn it down: Settings › Checks › Sensitivity, or `keepmum guard sensitivity injection|harm <level>`. Each level shows what it caught and flagged on keepmum's test sets. - **Prompt injection:** High (the default), Medium, Low or Lowest, or a number of your own. Medium catches 97% of the test injections instead of 99%, and flags 5% of security code instead of 7%. - **Harmful requests:** High, Medium (the default), Low or Lowest. Lower levels miss more harmful requests; see the README for each model's numbers. - **Check details on the Logs page.** Click a check's hit to see: - what happened and what to do next - the score against the threshold, the check's mode and model - where the request was going, and which local model answered - what was flagged and what you had asked, with every masked value shown as its type, like `‹EMAIL›`
The text is kept in memory only, never in the audit log or on disk, and only while **Text around values** is on (Settings › General › Logs page). The Outcome column now says Refused, Local, Replaced or Warned. - **Settings in panes.** Setup, Masking, Tools, Checks, General and Check this Mac, each on its own pane, in two columns on a wide window. - **A new installer window.** The DMG shows where to drag Keepmum, and the mounted disk carries Keepmum's icon.
## Fixes
- File names such as `guard-20261104-231405.md` are no longer taken for secrets. The model and the entropy check flagged some, which filled the Logs page with masked names that were never sensitive. A key whose format keepmum knows is still masked, even inside a file name. - Claude Code's AskUserQuestion results, which hold your own answers, are no longer checked for prompt injection. - Settings › Tools now shows progress on Trust again and Keep these, and an error if one fails, instead of doing nothing visible.
## Known limitations
- Local mode is only as good as your local model. A small one may repeat a planted instruction as advice, or help with what the harm check flagged. Use a capable model (8B or larger). - Lower sensitivity means fewer false alarms and fewer real catches; the harm check gives up catches quickly below Medium. - Shell commands still receive real values (so `git push` works), and your agent's local transcripts hold real values: keepmum protects what leaves your Mac, not what is stored on it.
Feedback and bug reports are welcome in [Issues](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum/issues).

item.title: keepmum 0.1.0a3
item.description:
The third alpha of keepmum adds a check on what comes back: the shell commands a model asks your agent to run. The flow diagram also shows what the optional checks did.
> **Alpha.** keepmum works end to end, but it has not been audited and things will change. Treat it as a safety layer, not a guarantee, and see [Limitations](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum#limitations).
## Install
1. Download `Keepmum-0.1.0a3.dmg` below, open it, and drag Keepmum into Applications. 2. Open Keepmum and follow **Settings › Setup**.
**From 0.1.0a2:** Keepmum updates itself if you allowed update checks (Settings › Updates › Check now). **From 0.1.0a1:** quit Keepmum and drag the new version into Applications, once.
Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
To check the download: `shasum -a 256 -c Keepmum-0.1.0a3.dmg.sha256`
## What's new
- **A risky-commands check (optional, off by default).** keepmum reads the shell commands in the model's replies before your agent sees them: Claude Code's Bash, Codex's shell tools, and Gemini CLI's `run_shell_command`. It checks them against seven rules: - a download run as a script (`curl … | sh`) - decoded text run as a script - deleting your home folder or the system - erasing a disk - a fork bomb - credential files sent over the network - environment variables sent over the network
**Warn** logs a hit and lets the command through. **Block** hands the agent, in its place, a command that prints why keepmum refused it and fails, so the model can explain or ask you. No model and no download: Settings › Checks › Risky commands, or `keepmum guard commands warn`. - **The checks in the flow diagram.** Requests sent with a warning get a **Flagged** band, and requests a check stopped get a **Refused** band, each naming which check. Blocked now means only keepmum's own refusals.
## Known limitations
- The commands check covers the clear cases. A command built to hide what it does gets past it; the rules on where real values may be sent still apply. - Official one-line installers (`curl … | bash`) are flagged too. If you install tools through your agent often, use warn rather than block. - Shell commands still receive real values (so `git push` works), and your agent's local transcripts hold real values: keepmum protects what leaves your Mac, not what is stored on it.
Feedback and bug reports are welcome in [Issues](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum/issues).

item.title: keepmum 0.1.0a2
item.description:
The second alpha of keepmum adds two optional checks that run on your Mac, a switch for personal data, and updates: from this version on, the app updates itself.
> **Alpha.** keepmum works end to end, but it has not been audited and things will change. Treat it as a safety layer, not a guarantee, and see [Limitations](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum#limitations).
## Install
1. Download `Keepmum-0.1.0a2.dmg` below, open it, and drag Keepmum into Applications. 2. Open Keepmum and follow **Settings › Setup**.
**From 0.1.0a1:** quit Keepmum, then drag the new version into Applications to replace it. That is needed once: 0.1.0a1 cannot update itself, and this version can.
Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. The app is signed and notarized by Apple.
To check the download: `shasum -a 256 -c Keepmum-0.1.0a2.dmg.sha256`
## What's new
- **Updates.** On its first launch the app asks whether to check for updates once a day. A check downloads keepmum's update list from github.com, so GitHub sees your IP address and keepmum's version; nothing else is sent. Updates are signed by keepmum and notarized by Apple, and both are checked before one is installed. Settings › Updates has "Check now", and can download and install updates automatically. - **A prompt-injection check (optional, off by default).** It looks at what tools return (web pages, files, MCP replies) for instructions planted for your agent. **Warn** logs a hit and sends the request; **Block** refuses it. It uses Horizon Labs' Prompt Injection Guard Small (Apache-2.0), a 164 MB download that runs locally on the GPU. - **A harm check (optional, off by default).** It looks at what you type for requests a company policy may not allow, and names their categories. Three model sizes are available: Small (164 MB, the default), Qwen3Guard 0.6B, and Qwen3Guard 4B (the most accurate). - **Settings › Checks** sets both checks up. What they flag shows on the Logs and Activity pages, and `keepmum guard` does the same on the command line. - **Personal data** has its own switch in the app and `keepmum pii on|off`. Every setting that used to need config.toml now has a place in the app.
## Known limitations
- The checks are an early warning on top of masking, not a replacement for it. The injection check flags about 9% of security writing that quotes attacks, so warn suits security work better than block. - Shell commands still receive real values (so `git push` works). The host check stops the common case, but a command built to hide where it sends things gets past it. Use a sandbox with a network allowlist alongside keepmum. - Your agent's local transcripts hold real values: keepmum protects what leaves your Mac, not what is stored on it.
Feedback and bug reports are welcome in [Issues](https://github.com/blueandhack/keepmum/issues).
